title: Anti-punitive feminism
summary: Justice, repair and alternatives to punishment.
body:
Course themes

  • A genealogy of anti-punitive feminism
  • Neoliberalism and security policy
  • Feminisms and the reactionary turn
  • Restorative and transformative justice
  • Community experiences of repair and conflict management

What will we work on?

Sharing tools to think about a feminist politics able to confront violence and build collective responses.

Context and approach

In recent decades, part of the feminist agenda has been built around expanding criminal law and calling for greater police and judicial intervention. The course looks at how this common sense was constructed and how it relates to neoliberalism and security policy.

Through readings and discussion of concrete experiences, we will explore the tensions between justice, repair and punishment, the instrumentalisation of victim protection, and the possibilities of restorative and transformative justice.
introduction: What happens when punishment becomes the main response to violence? A course to discuss punitive common sense and think about how to deal with conflict without reproducing the logics of control and exclusion.
